I have farmed this land in Quzhou for fifty years, and at seventy I trust my own eyes more than any textbook. With only three of us in the household — and my son working in a factory most of the year — I must choose crops that match my labor and the well irrigation I have. The wheat-maize rotation is my backbone: it is highly mechanized, gives two harvests a year from the same field, and the grain stores safely even if market prices dip. Cotton can earn good money, but it is back-breaking work and needs endless pesticide sprays, so I will limit it to a plot I can manage with my wife and a little hired help at picking.

I will put **16 mu into the wheat-maize double crop** and keep **4 mu for cotton**. For the wheat, I will sow an improved *Shimai* variety in mid-October after one pass with the rotary tiller. I have learned that piling on fertilizer wastes money and hurts the soil, so I will apply about **32 kg of nitrogen per mu**, with compound fertilizer providing roughly **20 kg of phosphorus** and **10 kg of potassium**. Wheat needs steady water, so I will irrigate four times — once in winter to guard against frost, and three times in spring at the critical growth stages. I will spray pesticides about four times to control weeds, aphids, and rust.

As soon as the wheat comes off in early June, I will plant a **hybrid maize** variety the same day, using **no-tillage** direct seeding to save time and fuel. Hybrid seed gives me the vigor and yield I need on this tight schedule. Maize needs less phosphorus here than wheat, so **25 kg of nitrogen** and about **7 kg each of phosphorus and potassium per mu** is sufficient. Two irrigations — one at jointing and one at grain-filling — will carry it through the summer heat.

For the **4 mu of cotton**, I will rotary-till in April and plant an improved *Guoxinmian* variety. Cotton demands balanced nutrition and relentless pest control, so I will apply **20 kg of nitrogen** and **15 kg each of phosphorus and potassium per mu**, and spray pesticides roughly sixteen times against bollworm, aphids, and mites. I will irrigate twice, timed at flowering and boll-setting. I expect my usual yields: about **1,050 kg/mu for wheat**, **1,150 kg/mu for maize**, and **550 kg/mu of seed cotton**.
